question: Which of the following steps in the data science lifecycle do not require MLOps to manage but DevOps suffices?
options: Bias detection|Model training & selection|Feature engineering|Champion and challenger model evaluation and promotion|Label drift detection
correct_answers: Feature engineering
explanation: Feature engineering is ordinary development/data-preparation work that DevOps can handle. The other choices explicitly concern ML-specific evaluation, promotion, bias or drift controls that require MLOps. MEMORIZE: DevOps builds software. MLOps adds controls for model/data behavior in production.

question: In what way can effective governance of ML systems be realized beyond just accuracy measurement?
options: Monitoring, Observability, Response|Continuous integration, Continuous Delivery, Operations|Logging, Tracing, Metrics Collection|Bias detection, Drift monitoring & Explainability|Regulatory risk, Reputational harm & Change management
correct_answers: Bias detection, Drift monitoring & Explainability
explanation: Bias, drift and explainability are explicitly ML-governance concerns that go beyond a single accuracy score. Monitoring/observability are operational mechanisms, not governance. MEMORIZE: Governance = BDE: Bias, Drift, Explainability.

question: Which of the following captures the 3 pillars of production operations?
options: Monitoring, Observability, Response|Detect, Understand, Act|CI, CD, MLSecOps|Explainability, Drift Monitoring, Bias Detection|Infrastructure, Software, Configuration
correct_answers: Monitoring, Observability, Response
explanation: The three-pillar production-operations framing is Monitoring, Observability and Response. Do not confuse production operations with CI/CD or ML-governance controls. MEMORIZE: MOR = Monitor, Observe, Respond.

question: Which of the below is not an example of a software-driven data source?
options: OLTP database that serves as the backend to a PHP application|OpenAI-hosted URL endpoint that serves your custom-trained GPT|Logs from containers|Docker manifest file|CML report in a Github repo
correct_answers: Docker manifest file
explanation: A Docker manifest is primarily deployment/image metadata or configuration, not a data source. Logs and reports are still data even though software generates them. MEMORIZE: Manifest describes the image. Logs/report describe what happened.

question: For which of the following use cases is an LLM NOT well suited?
options: Reasoning about macroeconomic implications of a country's finance policy|Answering targeted questions about features of a washing machine from its user manual|Performing rule-driven classification of scanned images submitted as supporting documents to a bank for ID proof and address proof categories|Incorporating dynamic learning about customer preferences for customer servicing|Building a risky driving alerting system using telematics data from trucks where sensors track location, movement, driving behaviour, and vehicle health
correct_answers: Building a risky driving alerting system using telematics data from trucks where sensors track location, movement, driving behaviour, and vehicle health
explanation: The use case is fundamentally a real-time structured telemetry/time-series alerting problem. A specialized ML/rules/time-series system is a more natural fit than an LLM. MEMORIZE: LLM = language/unstructured reasoning. High-rate numeric telemetry alerting = specialized systems.

question: The data schema comprises a Fact table (PurchaseEvent) recording purchases made by customers via various channels along with associated Dimension tables (Customer, Online, WhatsApp, CallCenter, OfflinePointOfSale, Product). How would you design the Feast data model to support ML development?
options: Every Dimension table is a Feast entity. The PurchaseEvent Fact table becomes a FeatureView|The PurchaseEvent Fact table becomes a Feast entity. Each Dimension table is a FeatureView with the Fact entity linked to it|The PurchaseEvent Fact table needs to be processed further to create useful features (e.g. using aggregations). That processed table becomes a FeatureView. Every Dimension table is a Feast entity linked to that FeatureView|Join the Fact and Dimension tables together to create one large denormalized table. Summarize into useful features. Make this the FeatureView. No entity required separately
correct_answers: The PurchaseEvent Fact table needs to be processed further to create useful features (e.g. using aggregations). That processed table becomes a FeatureView. Every Dimension table is a Feast entity linked to that FeatureView
explanation: Raw purchase events need to be transformed into useful time-aware features. Those become the FeatureView, while Customer, Channel and Product are natural entities. Do not automatically make the raw fact table the FeatureView. MEMORIZE: ENTITY = identity. FEATUREVIEW = usable features.

question: Which of the following statements regarding git are true?
options: git checkout -b branch will not work if the branch does not exist|A pull request is used to merge 2 branches|On git commit all collaborators in the repo can see the changes immediately|git push origin feature/my-cool-idea pushes code from the local branch to the local branch origin|On git pull all changes in the current branch are downloaded from remote
correct_answers: A pull request is used to merge 2 branches|On git pull all changes in the current branch are downloaded from remote
explanation: git checkout -b creates a new branch (A is false). Commit is local only (C is false). origin is a remote name, not a local branch (D is false). Pull fetches remote changes (E is true). A PR merges 2 branches (B is true). MEMORIZE: COMMIT stays local. PUSH sends. PULL receives.

question: Which of the below are part of what MLOps manages?
options: ML models|Not the actual LLM itself since that is large and proprietary, only its architecture|Data engineering code|Only small data since big data is not effectively managed via versioning systems|k8s (Kubernetes) configuration files
correct_answers: ML models|Data engineering code|k8s (Kubernetes) configuration files
explanation: MLOps covers model artifacts, data/feature engineering code and infrastructure/configuration. It is not limited to small data (D is false), nor does it exclude an LLM simply because it is large or proprietary (B is false). MEMORIZE: MLOps manages the ML system, not just the model.

question: Which of the below definitions of security attacks on ML systems are correct?
options: Identifying which patients data has been used in a heart attack prediction model is an example of membership inference attack|Cloning a live API and stealing away live traffic is an example of man-in-the-middle attack|Fooling a vehicle by making it understand red signals as orange is an example of evasion attack|Figuring out which facial patterns are known to cause a positive match in a criminal matching system is an example of inversion attack|Feeding wrong data samples is an example of enrichment attack
correct_answers: Identifying which patients data has been used in a heart attack prediction model is an example of membership inference attack|Fooling a vehicle by making it understand red signals as orange is an example of evasion attack|Figuring out which facial patterns are known to cause a positive match in a criminal matching system is an example of inversion attack
explanation: Membership inference asks whether a record was in training data (A). Evasion manipulates input to fool the model (C). Inversion infers sensitive information from model behavior (D). B and E do not match standard attack labels. MEMORIZE: MEMBERSHIP = training set. EVASION = input. INVERSION = infer.

question: Which of the following statements regarding model deployment are true?
options: Once a Docker image is created, the Dockerfile is no longer required to deploy the image|The Registry allows for having independent development machines where Docker images are created, separate from a common container execution environment like k8s|The annotation @app.post(/predict) tells FastAPI that this app can receive all HTTP request types for /predict|A K8s cluster takes time to spin up because containers are heavyweight and take time to deploy on host machines|A custom web service using FastAPI is better than a k8s cluster of containers only for fast iterations on development and testing|A pod is the smallest unit of deployment in k8s and comprises of one or more containers|The benefits of k8s over using plain Docker are ability to scale and have easier management of containers
correct_answers: Once a Docker image is created, the Dockerfile is no longer required to deploy the image|The Registry allows for having independent development machines where Docker images are created, separate from a common container execution environment like k8s|A custom web service using FastAPI is better than a k8s cluster of containers only for fast iterations on development and testing|A pod is the smallest unit of deployment in k8s and comprises of one or more containers|The benefits of k8s over using plain Docker are ability to scale and have easier management of containers
explanation: Built image runs without Dockerfile (A true). Registry decouples creation from execution (B true). @app.post is POST-specific only (C false). Containers are not heavyweight (D false). FastAPI good for fast dev (E true). Pod = smallest unit with 1+ containers (F true). K8s adds scaling/management (G true). MEMORIZE: IMAGE->REGISTRY->RUNTIME. POD=1+ containers.

question: A candidate claims LLMOps is significantly more complex than MLOps. As hiring manager, which arguments would you use to counter that?
options: Source data provenance and lineage tracking is the same effort for any type of model|Accuracy testing is the same for any type of model|Securing the model requires a similar level of work and tooling|Monitoring and responding requires the same level of hands-on expertise and time across any model type|Cost analysis and optimizations to be carried out are similar|Team collaboration and end-to-end ownership has similar responsibilities
correct_answers: Source data provenance and lineage tracking is the same effort for any type of model|Monitoring and responding requires the same level of hands-on expertise and time across any model type|Team collaboration and end-to-end ownership has similar responsibilities
explanation: Source-confirmed: Provenance/lineage (A), monitoring/response (D) and team collaboration/ownership (F) are comparable across model types. Accuracy testing (B) and cost analysis (E) differ substantially for LLMs. MEMORIZE: Same core ownership and operational responsibilities recur across model types.

question: A code-generation SaaS using GPT-5 has stagnant cost per dollar of sales despite revenue growth. As CPO, which mechanisms can you put in place within 1 month?
options: Instrument tracing and metrics collection to understand GPT usage in detail|Introduce product analytics, analyze least used features that use GPT heavily, and weed them out|Build custom replacements for all GPT usage using DeepSeek by leveraging distillation|Use self-hosted GPU hardware for the OpenAI usage to save on GPU costs|Identify repeat GPT querying patterns and introduce caching for such query-response pairs|Build quantized custom equivalents of GPT for simpler LLM usage using open source base models
correct_answers: Instrument tracing and metrics collection to understand GPT usage in detail|Identify repeat GPT querying patterns and introduce caching for such query-response pairs|Build quantized custom equivalents of GPT for simpler LLM usage using open source base models
explanation: Source-confirmed: Tracing/metrics reveals usage (A), caching removes repeated API calls (E), and quantized open-source equivalents reduce expensive hosted usage (F). Full replacement (C) and self-hosted GPUs for OpenAI (D) are not feasible in 1 month. MEMORIZE: TRACE, CACHE, QUANTIZE.

question: At a bank, ML serving servers are commodity Linux machines with Prometheus already instrumented. What is the minimum set of additional data needed for effective troubleshooting and governance?
options: Logs from the ML serving servers for detailed records of model executions|CPU and GPU utilization for model efficiency and scalability|Tracing across various servers for effective debugging across dependent services end-to-end|Kubernetes logs required for detailed troubleshooting|Metrics for every external requestor to assess security-related abuse|Kernel logs necessary to debug security loopholes in the Linux machines
correct_answers: Logs from the ML serving servers for detailed records of model executions|Tracing across various servers for effective debugging across dependent services end-to-end
explanation: Source-confirmed: Prometheus already supplies metrics. Minimum additional signals are detailed logs (A) and tracing across dependent servers (C). No Kubernetes exists so D is irrelevant. MEMORIZE: Minimum missing observability = Logs + Traces.

question: Which of the following steps is NOT recommended in a CI/CD approach for classical ML models? (Steps I through X listed in question)
options: I. Use Git-flow & Deploy Model lifecycle patterns|II. Use Github, CML and MLflow as tooling|III. Commit code in feature branch|IV. Automated approval from feature branch to develop branch|V. CD pipeline after merging, to run the new model in staging env|VI. Automated step of running on staging & measuring model performance|VII. CI when raising a PR for merging with main/release branch|VIII. Manual approval to merge with main|IX. CD pipeline after merging, to train the new model in prod env|X. Promote the trained model directly to production usage
correct_answers: I. Use Git-flow & Deploy Model lifecycle patterns|IV. Automated approval from feature branch to develop branch|X. Promote the trained model directly to production usage
explanation: Source-confirmed: Steps I, IV and X are NOT-recommended. The paper flags the Deploy Model lifecycle pattern, automatic feature-to-develop approval, and direct promotion to production. MEMORIZE: Q177 = I + IV + X.

question: Current model: main branch only, everything coded on main and pushed to remote. What changes will you introduce for Git-flow?
options: Use a develop branch separate from main to separate new development from production code|Do not push to remote from local until a pull request is raised and approved|Only code critical bug fixes directly in main, not new features|Use tags for each new version of the code in main|Create a separate branch for each feature, and once tested, merge into develop using a pull request
correct_answers: Use a develop branch separate from main to separate new development from production code|Use tags for each new version of the code in main|Create a separate branch for each feature, and once tested, merge into develop using a pull request
explanation: Git-flow separates dev from prod (A), uses feature branches merged via PRs (E), and version tagging (D). B is too restrictive. C is wrong because hotfix branches handle urgent fixes. MEMORIZE: FEATURE->DEVELOP->RELEASE->MAIN.

question: Management uses Excel to manually extrapolate revenue projections. Sales over-reports, finance under-reports. Which activities constitute your strategy?
options: Use a PyTorch-based deep learning model for programmatic forecasting|Use one of the available forecasting functions within Excel instead of manual extrapolations|Feed the forecast directly with data from both sales and finance teams|"Compute a common set of features that both teams agree on
correct_answers: including revenue
explanation: using Feast and feed into the forecast"
tags: Use one of the available forecasting functions within Excel instead of manual extrapolations|"Compute a common set of features that both teams agree on
column8: using Feast and feed into the forecast"
column9: Use existing Excel forecasting function (B) and establish shared governed feature definitions via Feast (D). Deep learning (A) is overkill. Combining conflicting feeds (C) does not solve the definition problem. MEMORIZE: First fix the DATA CONTRACT, then improve the MODEL.

question: Your prototype is approved for production. Which step ensures model selection and hyperparameter decisions are logged for future data scientists?
options: Configure a central MLflow server for tracking every experiment and hyperparameter tuning|Use logging through Python print commands and rely on container log collection|Use sklearn's automl to avoid going through various model types or hyperparameters|Create a Github repo, push for each change, and use CML for logging model metrics|Containerize using Docker and run using k8s on GKE which brings all necessary logging
correct_answers: Configure a central MLflow server for tracking every experiment and hyperparameter tuning
explanation: MLflow is designed for experiment tracking, including parameters, metrics and artifacts across runs. Git records code history but is not a replacement for systematic experiment tracking. MEMORIZE: MLflow = What did we try, with which parameters, and what happened?

question: An AI entrepreneur built an LLM from Reddit/X data for human rights news on WhatsApp using Gemma2-9B, hand-engineered 1000 samples, RAG with daily news, and assignment-type GPU. What problems did consumers encounter in the first month?
options: The LLM could not search through daily news documents in the RAG database|The LLM hallucinated since there was no data curation in pretraining finetuning or RAG|The LLM started giving misinformed and toxic opinions since there was no screening for ingested data|The LLM became stale since it was built using older data while latest news was only usable by retrieval|The LLM kept crashing intermittently due to lack of batching underprovisioned resources and inefficient resource usage
correct_answers: The LLM hallucinated since there was no data curation in pretraining finetuning or RAG|The LLM started giving misinformed and toxic opinions since there was no screening for ingested data|The LLM kept crashing intermittently due to lack of batching underprovisioned resources and inefficient resource usage
explanation: Raw social data without curation creates quality/safety problems (B, C). Assignment-sized GPU fails under demand without batching/resource management (E). RAG supplies fresh retrieved information so D is not the problem. MEMORIZE: RAG = fresh retrieval, not fresh weights.

question: As CDO, you must minimize security risks for data used in ML production models fed from a central data lake. Which risks are worth calling out?
options: Data cannot be trusted unless provenance and data lineage back to the source is established|Each custom pipeline introduces security risks in feature engineering code. Centralizing features into a single feature store minimizes code-level risks|The data lake cannot be trusted. Extending pipelines all the way back to source ensures full traceability|Drift in data means models become outdated so retraining minimizes model irrelevance risk|ML models are artifacts that need protection. Encrypt them and store in secure model registries|Gatekeep the model serving infrastructure to minimize risks from probing and leakage
correct_answers: Data cannot be trusted unless provenance and data lineage back to the source is established|Each custom pipeline introduces security risks in feature engineering code. Centralizing features into a single feature store minimizes code-level risks|ML models are artifacts that need protection. Encrypt them and store in secure model registries|Gatekeep the model serving infrastructure to minimize risks from probing and leakage
explanation: Source-confirmed: Provenance/lineage (A), centralized features reduce code risks (B), models need encryption/secure registries (E), serving access should be controlled (F). Extending pipelines to source (C) increases duplicated logic. D is not selected by the source. MEMORIZE: Q182 = A + B + E + F.

question: An online portal runs a midnight batch fraud model. Now sees 1 listing/second and wants to flag fraud within 5 minutes. Which changes are necessary?
options: Enable the streaming inference mode in scikit-learn|Containerize the model using Docker and execute using k8s|Feed listings in near real-time into Kafka develop stream processing using Spark Streaming and invoke the model as an API|Attach a GPU accelerator and switch to PyTorch|Run the model on the edge by deploying the Jupyter notebook on the web server
correct_answers: Containerize the model using Docker and execute using k8s|Feed listings in near real-time into Kafka develop stream processing using Spark Streaming and invoke the model as an API
explanation: Midnight batch cannot meet 5-minute SLA. Near-real-time ingestion via Kafka/Spark Streaming required (C) and containerized serving provides suitable deployment (B). Scikit-learn has no streaming inference mode (A). GPU/PyTorch doesnt fix batch architecture (D). MEMORIZE: SLA first -> architecture second -> hardware last.

question: MLOps newbie sets up CI with DVC on RHEL server and CML with Github Actions (trigger on push, ubuntu-latest runner). What problems can you anticipate?
options: CML action will fail because there is no token set to interact with Github|Github action runner cannot run large workloads so model training will fail|Github action will fail because RHEL doesnt match the Ubuntu container in the workflow|Since action triggers on every push each branch change triggers full model training running into free tier limits|Since action triggers on every push only the merge into main runs the model losing CI benefits|Github action doesnt specify any tests to run so the primary objective of CI is missing
correct_answers: CML action will fail because there is no token set to interact with Github|Github action runner cannot run large workloads so model training will fail|Since action triggers on every push each branch change triggers full model training running into free tier limits|Github action doesnt specify any tests to run so the primary objective of CI is missing
explanation: Source-confirmed: Missing GitHub token (A), insufficient hosted-runner capacity (B), expensive training on every push (D), and no actual test step (F). RHEL vs Ubuntu mismatch (C) is irrelevant since workflow runs in GitHub's hosted environment. MEMORIZE: CI workflow audit = AUTH + COMPUTE + TRIGGER + TEST.
